Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde.short_definition: Showing one warm, admired face to the world and another harsh one to a particular person, so nobody else sees the treatment that person receives.
Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde.core_meaning: Showing one warm, admired face to the world and another harsh one to a particular person, so nobody else sees the treatment that person receives.
Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde.expanded_definition: The name comes from a well-known story about one man with two opposite selves. In everyday life it describes a split between how someone behaves in front of others and how they behave alone with one person. Everyone is a little different in public and private, so that alone means little. It deserves a closer look when the private side is harsh, the public side is admired, and the gap leaves the receiving person with no one who would believe them.
Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde.plain_language_summary: Everyone outside the home sees a kind, friendly person. Alone with you, they are cold or cruel. Because no one else sees it, you start to doubt yourself and wonder who will believe you.
Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde.why_this_matters: The target has no witnesses. The version other people know makes their account of the other version sound implausible, including to themselves.
what_it_is: A sharp gap between conduct in front of others and conduct in private, aimed at one person or a small circle.
Often shown in how the person is described by others: helpful, funny, generous, reliable.
Made harder to name when good phases between the harsh ones feel like proof that the harsh phases were a mistake.
Seen in couples, parent and child, bosses and employees, and religious or community leaders.
what_it_sounds_like: A friend says, "But he's so lovely whenever I see him. Are you sure?"
In front of guests: "Isn't she wonderful? I'd be lost without her." At home, hours later, a cold silence.
"No one is going to believe you. Look how everyone sees me."
A pleasant, joking voice at the party; a flat, hostile one on the drive home.
"You've got everyone fooled into thinking I'm the bad one."
Warm texts to your family, curt and critical ones to you.
what_it_is_not: A shy or tired person who is quiet at home and animated at work, with no harshness toward anyone in either place.
A professional who is polished with clients and grumpy after a long day, but who owns it and repairs it.
Someone with a hard private temper who is open about it, so others also know and can judge.
A relationship where outsiders simply have not seen ordinary arguments, which many couples keep to themselves.
A person who is quiet and guarded in public but relaxed and kind at home, which is the reverse of this split.
this_may_be_it_when: How they treat you when others are around is so different that you are unsure which one is real.
The hostile side shows up only where nobody else would see or hear it.
Friends or relatives have said they find the person lovely, and you have stopped bringing it up.
The kindness shows up after the harshness, in a way that makes you doubt your memory of it.
They have said, or you believe, that no one would take your word over theirs.
this_may_not_be_it_when: People close to you have also seen the harsh side and do not find your account surprising.
The private behavior is irritable but not cruel, and gets owned and apologized for.
The difference is one of volume or formality, such as being relaxed at home and polite at work.
You are the only person they are harsh to, but a specific, understandable conflict sits behind it and both of you can talk about it.
The warm public manner is also how they treat you when you are alone together.
innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: People do act more formally in public, so a warmer social manner does not hide anything by itself.
Stress from work or health can make home the place where someone's patience runs out, without any plan behind it.
A person may hold back private arguments from friends for reasons of embarrassment or loyalty.
common_false_positives: A teenager who is chatty with friends and withdrawn at the dinner table.
A teacher who is relaxed with students and strict in staff meetings.
Two partners with different moods after the children are asleep, both of them tired and frayed.
discernment_questions: Would people who know them be shocked, or just surprised, to hear how they speak to you in private?
Is the harshness reserved for the times when no one can hear it?
Do the warm phases ever involve you saying that the cruel moments were real, or do they quietly erase them?
Have you stopped telling anyone because you expect not to be believed?
Do you hold dated notes, messages or recordings that show the other side, and do you feel you need them?
less_concerning_if: The difference is mostly in volume and formality, and nothing in private is hurtful.
Close friends or family have seen both sides and are not surprised by your account.
Hard moments in private are named and repaired afterward, and do not return in the same form.
more_concerning_if: You have been told directly that you would not be believed, or that you would look unstable if you spoke.
The private harshness comes with monitoring of your phone, money or movements.
They contact your friends or family to describe you as difficult before you speak to them.
pattern_over_time_signs: You find yourself deciding what to share with others by how likely they are to say, "But he seems so nice."
Photos and posts show a happy home that does not match your own account of it.
Your sense of which version is real keeps flipping with the weather in the house.
You have started to keep your own record of events because nobody else holds one.
Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde.repair_check: Change would look like the harsh side no longer needing a hiding place: they treat you the same when unobserved, do not object when you speak to others about what happened, and stop asking you to keep the private version private. A kinder week with the public face intact shows only a pleasant phase.
Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde.boundary_respect_check: Notice whether your request is honored when nobody is watching. A boundary kept only in front of guests and dropped at home tells you what it is worth. Compare early weeks with later ones: do the private behaviors continue, even once the public manner has softened?
Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde.psychological_mechanism: When most people see only the pleasant version, a person on the receiving end can start weighing their own account against everyone else's, and tends to lose. Good phases may feed hope that the harsh phases were not real, while the private ones leave no proof. Doubt about what happened, and about who would listen, can keep a person quiet.
Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde.possible_impact_on_receiver: People describe isolation that feels odd because they are surrounded by people who admire the other person. Some report rehearsing their account for years without telling it, and feeling an odd guilt for describing someone others like. Others say they came to dread praise of the person, and found it hardest to be congratulated for having such a partner.

response_options.soft_clarification: Say what you notice about the difference without arguing the character: "You were gentle with my sister today, and this morning you spoke to me very differently. I'd like to understand that."
response_options.firm_boundary: Hold the same standard in both settings: "How I am spoken to should not depend on who is in the room."
response_options.disengagement: Stop trying to prove the private side to people who like the public one, and keep your own dated notes where the other person cannot read them.
response_options.support_seeking: Tell one person who can listen without trying to fix or defend, such as a counselor, a domestic abuse advocate, or a friend outside the shared circle.
response_options.workplace_or_professional: At work, write down dates, words and witnesses, and bring the record to HR or an ombuds, since a charming manner in meetings will not show up on its own.

Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde.boundary_script: "I want to be spoken to at home the way I'm spoken to in front of guests. Could we ask someone we both trust to sit in on this conversation?"
Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde.safety_note: A split like this can sit alongside controlling behavior, threats, or physical harm that stays hidden from outsiders. Warning signs are fear of what happens after guests leave, being told you would not be believed, or having your phone, money or contacts checked. Tell a domestic abuse advocate about it first, and keep records somewhere private and out of the home.
misuse_warning: Calling a person a Jekyll and Hyde because they were short with you after a hard day makes ordinary mood shifts into a case against their character. The label needs a sustained gap, not a bad evening.
Using it to tell friends that a well-liked person is secretly cruel, on the basis of your side alone, can spread a verdict that the evidence cannot yet support.
Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde.how_to_distinguish_from_related: Contempt is disgust toward you and can show in public and private alike; this one depends on a gap between the two. Intimidation implies a cost for not complying and needs no split of faces. Emotional Invalidation dismisses what you feel. Here the harsh treatment may be quite plain, and what is distinctive is that you have no audience who knows the private version.

Identity Erosion.short_definition: The slow loss of your own tastes, opinions, habits and friendships inside a relationship, until the person you were earlier is hard to find.
Identity Erosion.core_meaning: The slow loss of your own tastes, opinions, habits and friendships inside a relationship, until the person you were earlier is hard to find.
Identity Erosion.expanded_definition: This is something a person carries rather than something one party does in a single moment. Over months or years, preferences narrow toward what the other person likes, old friendships fade, and opinions get shelved to keep things smooth. Everyone changes in a close relationship, and some of it is chosen and welcome. The concern is a change that runs one way, that you did not decide on, and that leaves you unsure what you would choose alone.
Identity Erosion.plain_language_summary: You look up and cannot say what you like, what you think, or who your friends are anymore, because most of it has been shaped around someone else.
Identity Erosion.why_this_matters: Losing your own preferences and people makes it harder to judge a situation, to leave one, or even to describe what you want. Without a self to measure against, a person can drift further from the support that would help.
what_it_is: A gradual shift in tastes, opinions, clothes, hobbies and routines to match someone else's.
A shrinking circle, in which friends and family are seen less because there is less room or less welcome for them.
Often a series of small accommodations, each reasonable alone, that add up to a different life.
A state felt from the inside, usually noticed later when something, such as a song or a photo, shows a gap.
what_it_sounds_like: "I don't know, whatever you want is fine."
"I used to love painting, but I haven't picked up a brush in years."
"I haven't seen my college friends since we moved in together. It just sort of happened."
"What do I think about it? I'd have to check what we think."
Finding old playlists and not recognizing a single song as yours.
"I can't remember what I wore before I met them."
what_it_is_not: Growing and changing in a good partnership, where both people try new things and both keep parts of their old selves.
A move, a new job or a new baby that naturally replaces old routines and friends for a while.
Falling out of an old hobby because you lost interest, with nobody encouraging that.
Choosing to spend more time with your partner or family and less with a wide circle, with nothing in the relationship asking for it.
The ordinary blur of early adulthood, when many people are still working out who they are.
this_may_be_it_when: You can name specific things you loved before the relationship that you now avoid or feel awkward about.
You pre-check how a friend, hobby or opinion will be received before you act on it.
Time with your old friends has dropped, and the reasons you give sound like excuses.
You agree out loud with views you privately do not hold, mostly to avoid conflict.
Imagining a day on your own makes you realize you do not know what you would do.
this_may_not_be_it_when: You can say why each change happened and would make the same choice again.
Your old friends are still in your life, though you see them less because of distance.
You have taken on your partner's hobby and still do things that only you enjoy.
Your views have shifted because you thought them through, and you can argue for them.
Changes are matched by your partner's own changes, and both of you say the relationship has made you more yourself.
innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: Taste and opinion shift naturally across a decade, relationship or not.
Partners often trade interests and enjoy it.
A busy stage of life, with young children or demanding work, pushes out hobbies and friendships for reasons that have nothing to do with anyone's influence.
Someone coming out of a difficult stretch may be rebuilding their sense of self slowly.
common_false_positives: Moving across the country and losing daily contact with old friends.
Giving up an old sport after an injury.
Choosing a quieter life after years of being very social, and being glad of it.
discernment_questions: Can you list three things you liked before this relationship that you no longer do, and do you miss them?
Who decided that those things should change, and did you agree at the time?
If you were making plans only for yourself, what would you pick?
Which people do you see less now, and is that your choice?
When you express an opinion, do you check first how it will land?
less_concerning_if: You can still say what you like and think, even when it differs from your partner's.
Your friendships continue, in some form, and are welcome in the home.
You enjoy the new habits and can trace how you came to them.
more_concerning_if: Your own preferences are met with sighs, mockery or silence, so you stop voicing them.
Money, transport or schedules are arranged so that you cannot easily see other people.
You are afraid to say what you actually want, even in small matters.
pattern_over_time_signs: Photos from a few years ago look like someone you have to introduce to new friends.
Your answers to "what do you want to do?" start with a pause and the other person's name.
You find yourself defending the changes when a friend asks about them, before they have criticized anything.
Small pleasures that were yours alone, such as a morning run or a book club, drop away without a decision.
Identity Erosion.repair_check: Self-repair check: has any small piece of you returned? A hobby picked up again, a friend called back, an opinion said aloud and survived. Rebuilding tends to come in such small acts rather than a single decision, and a weekend of reinvention that fades by Monday is not the same as one.
Identity Erosion.boundary_respect_check: When you give yourself space to choose something small, such as a meal, a song or a Saturday plan, do you let yourself have it? Or does a habit of checking first take over before you notice? Notice how quickly the old reflex returns.
Identity Erosion.psychological_mechanism: Adapting to another person's likes and moods can be a way of keeping a relationship steady, and it tends to feel like love or flexibility while it is happening. Each accommodation is small, so no single one prompts a second look. Over time, a person's own preferences get less practice, and they can become harder to hear.
Identity Erosion.possible_impact_on_receiver: People describe an odd grief for someone who is still alive, a flatness when asked what they like, and a fear that nothing of them is left. Some say the loss showed itself only after the relationship ended, when the quiet gave them no cues. Guilt for even noticing it is common.

response_options.soft_clarification: Share a small, specific thing with your partner: "I miss going to my pottery class. I'd like to start again on Thursdays."
response_options.firm_boundary: Keep one thing as yours without making an announcement of it, such as a weekly call with a friend, and treat it as settled for yourself.
response_options.disengagement: Take small steps back toward things that were yours, such as a long-ignored hobby, and let them rebuild without needing anyone's permission.
response_options.support_seeking: Get in touch with one old friend or relative and ask what they remember about you. Their account can help you remember your own.
response_options.workplace_or_professional: If this is happening at work, such as a team that rewards sameness, keep notes on the projects and ideas that were yours, and talk to a mentor about reclaiming them.

Identity Erosion.boundary_script: Self-support script: "What I like and think counts, even when I can't say it out loud yet. I can start with one small choice today that is only mine."
Identity Erosion.safety_note: On its own this is a loss to notice, not an emergency. It becomes more serious if your friends, money, phone or travel are being limited, or if disagreeing brings anger, threats or silence for days. A domestic abuse advocate or counselor can help you think this through privately, at a pace that is safe for you.
misuse_warning: Telling a friend that they have lost themselves in a relationship, when they say they are happy, can feel like a verdict and push them away. Offer your observation once and keep the door open.
Using the phrase to explain every change in a partner, such as a new hobby, can turn growth into a charge against the person they love.
Identity Erosion.how_to_distinguish_from_related: Contempt shows disgust at you, and nothing need be said about you here, because this is a slow fading of preferences that may involve no criticism at all. Emotional Invalidation rules your feelings inadmissible, whereas the loss in this entry is of knowing what you want. Intimidation works through implied consequences, and none are needed.

Public Humiliation.short_definition: Embarrassing or belittling a person in front of others so that the audience adds to the sting and the person is lowered in everyone's eyes.
Public Humiliation.core_meaning: Embarrassing or belittling a person in front of others so that the audience adds to the sting and the person is lowered in everyone's eyes.
Public Humiliation.expanded_definition: What sets this apart from private criticism is the audience. A correction, a joke at someone's expense, a revealed secret or a story told against them weighs more with witnesses. Feedback given in public is sometimes unavoidable, so context matters. It raises concern when the audience seems to be part of the point, when the same words would be gentler in private, and when it keeps landing on one person.
Public Humiliation.plain_language_summary: You are put down, corrected or laughed at in front of other people, in a way that would have been handled differently in private. The audience is what makes it hurt.
Public Humiliation.why_this_matters: An audience makes the injury durable in a way private criticism is not: everyone present carries a version of it afterwards, including the person it was about.
what_it_is: Criticism, ridicule or exposure delivered where other people can see or hear it.
Forms include a correction in a meeting, a story told against you at dinner, or a post or group message that shames you.
More lasting than a private remark, because the witnesses remember it and the target remembers them remembering.
Seen in workplaces, classrooms, families, friend groups and online.
what_it_sounds_like: "Let me show everyone how it should have been done."
"Tell them what you did last weekend. Go on, it's hilarious."
A manager reading out your error in a team call, with your name attached.
"Oh, don't mind her, she never gets the details right."
A group chat message that quotes something private you said, with laughing faces.
"Do you want to tell them, or shall I?"
what_it_is_not: Necessary and time-sensitive feedback sometimes has to be given where others happen to be, and settings where feedback is normal and applied evenly to everybody are humiliating nobody.
An awkward moment can be nothing more than poor timing.
A public award or roast that the person agreed to and enjoys.
A teacher or coach correcting a technique in front of the group, in a setting where everyone expects it and nobody is mocked.
A story told with affection that the person is happy to have told, and which they might tell themselves.
this_may_be_it_when: The criticism is harsher when there are people around than it is alone with you.
Private things, such as a mistake or a secret, are used in front of others.
The same person is picked out in group settings more than others.
You see others glance at you or look away after it happens.
You were not given a chance to hear it in private first, though one was possible.
this_may_not_be_it_when: The feedback is the same for everyone and given in a way that is meant to be useful.
It was an emergency or a safety issue that needed fixing straight away.
You agreed to the format, such as a review session where all work is critiqued.
The speaker followed up privately to check how you felt and repaired it.
The comment was clumsy but kind in intent, and the person was visibly sorry.
innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: A busy meeting or live session leaves no time for private notes, and a quick correction may be the only option.
Some cultures and teams treat open correction as normal and respectful.
A person telling a funny story may not realize you find it embarrassing.
common_false_positives: A choir director correcting a section's timing.
A friend sharing an old photo that you also find funny now.
A manager reading out a company-wide error without naming anyone.
discernment_questions: Would the same words have been said in private, in the same way?
Did the audience seem to matter to the person speaking?
Is the same person the target again and again?
Was anything I had told in confidence used?
After it happened, did the person check in or acknowledge it?
less_concerning_if: Everyone is treated the same, and the setting makes public correction expected.
The person speaks to you in private afterward and makes it right.
The topic was a work task, and no personal detail was used.
more_concerning_if: Private information, like health, money or family trouble, is brought out in front of others.
The audience is chosen, such as your family, your team or your online followers.
Complaining about it leads to more of it, or to being told you embarrassed yourself.
pattern_over_time_signs: You begin to dread gatherings, meetings or group chats where this person will be present.
You find yourself preparing your answers in advance, to avoid being caught out in front of others.
Other people start to treat you as the butt of the joke, taking their cue from the way you are treated.
You speak less in groups, and your contributions are noticed less.
Public Humiliation.repair_check: Meaningful change would show in public as well as in private: the person corrects you, if they must, in a way that does not expose you, and speaks up for you when others laugh. Apologizing in a private message while repeating the behavior in front of others leaves the audience part unchanged.
Public Humiliation.boundary_respect_check: Ask for correction to happen one on one, then see what the next group setting brings. Is your request kept when other people are present, which is the moment it matters most? Or does the next public remark show it was put aside?
Public Humiliation.psychological_mechanism: People are highly attuned to how their group sees them, and being lowered in front of others is a hit to standing, not only to feelings. Witnesses add to it by laughing, going quiet or looking away. A person may begin to expect it, and the dread alone can change how they speak and act around others.
Public Humiliation.possible_impact_on_receiver: People describe heat in the face, loss of words, replaying the moment for days, and avoiding the people who saw it. Some say the worst part was a bystander's silence. Many talk about shrinking in later meetings, and about checking whether anyone still remembers.

response_options.soft_clarification: Ask for privacy next time, in a matter-of-fact tone: "If there's a problem with my work, I'd rather hear it one on one."
response_options.firm_boundary: Stop it in the room if you can: "I'd like to talk about this privately, not in front of the group."
response_options.disengagement: Leave the room, the chat or the table for a few minutes without explanation, and return only when the subject has moved on.
response_options.support_seeking: Talk to someone who was there, and ask what they saw and heard. Knowing that a witness found it unfair can lift the doubt you carry.
response_options.workplace_or_professional: Write down the date, the setting, the words used and who was present, then take the record to HR, a union rep, or a manager one level up.

Public Humiliation.boundary_script: "I'm glad to hear your feedback on my work. I'd just like to have it in private, not in front of the team."
Public Humiliation.safety_note: Public humiliation is mostly about standing and dignity, not physical danger. That changes if the humiliation includes intimate images or details shared without consent, threats to expose you, or follows you from a household to online spaces. Then save the evidence, report it to the platform or the police, and ask a legal aid service or an advocate about the next step.
misuse_warning: Calling a fair, public correction humiliation can let real problems with performance go unaddressed. The label fits when the audience is the point, not when the venue is.
Telling a group that someone humiliated you, as a way to turn people against them, can become a humiliation of its own.
Public Humiliation.how_to_distinguish_from_related: Shame Installation works on your sense of being fundamentally inadequate and can happen in private, whereas this relies on witnesses. Contempt is disgust that may not need an audience at all. Humor at your expense can be one means of humiliating someone, but humiliation can also come through corrections, revealed secrets or group messages.
